title: Identification of Anoikis-related potential biomarkers and therapeutic drugs in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension via bioinformatics analysis and in vitro experiment.
summary: Bioinformatics and machine-learning analyses of CTEPH patient/control transcriptomics identify candidate anoikis-related biomarkers, followed by in-vitro experiments.
ai_technology: GEO cohort (14 CTEPH, 4 controls) is used for gene-network and candidate selection; the paper reports cell experiments for selected markers.
organization: Department of Emergency, Henan Provincial People's Hospital, Zhengzhou, Henan, China

evidence.tested: Bioinformatics and machine-learning analyses of CTEPH patient/control transcriptomics identify candidate anoikis-related biomarkers, followed by in-vitro experiments.
evidence.unknown: Results are limited to the reported models, cohorts, datasets or experiments; broader generalization and clinical or operational benefit were not established.
evidence.ai_role: GEO cohort (14 CTEPH, 4 controls) is used for gene-network and candidate selection; the paper reports cell experiments for selected markers.
